title: Live stream: strict CBOR decoding, deterministic encoding
description:
Epic mimid-e64f; docs/design/binary-live-stream.md §3, §9 question 5; AGENTS.md "Decode strictly".

Chosen (Mark, 2026-11-20): strict decoding. Reject duplicate keys, indefinite-length items, non-shortest integers and trailing bytes; accept any key order.

Details chosen by the agent for mimid-e64f (INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC):
- Lengths must be shortest too (they are integers in RFC 8949 §3).
- Text must be valid UTF-8 (RFC 8949 §3.1 major type 3).
- Floats, tags, undefined and simple values other than false, true and null are refused: the protocol uses none. Unknown map members are kept and round-trip unchanged (AGENTS.md).
- Nesting deeper than a named constant is refused.
- Encoding uses the RFC 8949 §4.2.1 core deterministic order (keys sorted by their encoded bytes), so one value has one encoding and fixtures can be cross-checked with Python cbor2 canonical=True.
